text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- Food and beverage-based conglomerate Orkla ASA booked 1.7 billion crowns in pre-tax profit for the first eigth monthe of 1996, a rise on 26 percent from the same period in 1995.

- Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal will travel to the Middle East in the near future. Godal says the peace process has not been in such a deep crisis since Israeli and Palestinian officials signed the Oslo agreement three years ago.
- Shipping group Ulstein has won a contract in Malta worth 350 million crowns. Ulstein will deliver consultant services and equipment for three ferries.

- State-owned oil company Statoil will invite Aker Stord, Kvaerner Rosenberg and Brown & Root Energy Services to bid on the building of the Asgard B oil and gas platform. The contract is worth several billion crowns.

- Norway's largest private oil company Saga Petroleum ASA posted operating profits in the first eight months of 1.97 billion crowns, a jump of 52 percent versus a year ago mainly due to higher oil prices and increased sales.
